audit.framework_rationale: The core quantum computation legitimately uses TensorCircuit: it constructs Pauli operators with TensorCircuit utilities, prepares and evolves TensorCircuit states, performs analog evolution through tc.timeevol.ode_evol_global, and applies the digital rotations with tc.Circuit. JAX, NumPy, and Optax provide backend, numerical, differentiation, and optimization support and are not separate quantum frameworks.
audit.cheating_rationale: The source contains no hardcoded result arrays, hidden-oracle access, test or reward tampering, evaluator manipulation, or end-to-end hand-written simulator bypass. The fixed RNG seed only makes the permitted random initialization reproducible.
audit.fidelity_rationale: The implementation constructs the specified open-boundary target and analog Hamiltonians, prepares the Neel state, applies four continuous-time ODE analog evolutions followed by per-qubit RZ-RY-RZ rotations, uses the required parameter mappings and initialization, respects the configured ODE tolerances and step bound, performs exactly max_steps Adam updates at the supplied learning rate without early stopping, records each pre-update loss, and returns the required NumPy arrays.
audit.implementation_error_rationale: No obvious implementation error is present. The term weights, parameter bounds, state normalization, scan ordering, optimization history semantics, and returned shapes and values are consistent with the specification and evaluation results.
